parts.text:
I would like to adjust steps 5 and 6 of the quad calibration flow for better user experience.

- In step 5, for the measurements entering section, the order should be (CAD screenshot/diagram -> corresponding real-world photo -> textbox) per each axis so that the user can be given maximum visual context prior to measuring and entering each value.
- In step 6, I would like to remove the Before you measure and How to measure sections entirely, making it just the measurements and entry section (step 5 provides enough context that the user should be able to replicate it on step 6 without duplicated assistance).
- In addition, I would like to simplify the text entry in step 6 to be a table-like structure with the rows being the axes and the columns being the inner/outer; this will compact down the page and make text entry easier. This will likely involve removing the current images and labels which currently exist in the text entry section on this page.

     1	# Vite facts verified in this repo
     2	
     3	## Library mode always inlines assets (Vite 8)
     4	`node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js` → `shouldInline()`:
     5	```js
     6	if (buildPluginContext) {
     7	  if (environment.config.build.lib) return true;   // lib mode ALWAYS inlines
     8	  if (buildPluginContext.getModuleInfo(id)?.isEntry) return false;
     9	}
    10	...
    11	if (assetsInlineLimit === 0) return content.length < 0  // never
    12	```
    13	Consequence: `vite build --lib` turns every asset referenced via `new URL(..., import.meta.url)`
    14	into a base64 data URI, **ignoring `build.assetsInlineLimit: 0`**. A widget with 1.3MB of STLs
    15	would balloon into a multi-MB JS file and the download button would hand back a `data:` URL.
    16	
    17	**Chosen approach:** build the custom element with a plain (non-lib) build and an explicit
    18	Rollup input (`build.rollupOptions.input = { 'truss-calibrator': 'src/element/truss-calibrator.ts' }`),
    19	which emits real asset files next to the chunk and rewrites `new URL(..., import.meta.url)`
    20	references base-relatively when `base: './'`.
    21	
    22	## `new URL(asset, import.meta.url)`
    23	- Processed at build time only when the path is a **static string literal**.
    24	- In dev/test (Vitest) it resolves to an **absolute dev-server URL** (`http://localhost:3000/src/...`),
    25	  so tests must not assume a `file:` scheme or a relative pathname.
    26	- In a build with `base: './'` it emits a relative reference that resolves against the script URL.
    27	
    28	## CSS for shadow DOM
    29	Use `import css from './x.css?inline'` — returns the CSS text in JS. Avoids lib-mode CSS file
    30	emission entirely and lets the shadow root adopt it.
    31	
    32	## Solid event delegation is broken inside a shadow root — MUST disable
    33	`vite-plugin-solid` defaults to delegating events: it registers one listener per event name on
    34	`document` and finds the handler via a `$click`-style property on the element, starting from
    35	`event.target`. Across a shadow boundary the browser **retargets `event.target` to the host**, so
    36	the walk never reaches the element that was clicked and **every control in the widget is inert**.
    37	
    38	- Fix: `solid({ solid: { delegateEvents: false } })` in `vite.config.ts` (attaches real listeners).
    39	- **jsdom does not retarget for document-level listeners**, so the whole unit suite stays green
    40	  while the built bundle is dead. Only a real browser click exposes it.
    41	- Guard: a build-output test asserting the chunk contains no `$<event>` markers and does contain
    42	  `addEventListener("click")`. Verified the guard fails when delegation is switched back on.
    43	- Reproduce/debug in a browser: `page.evaluate` → `sr.querySelector('button').click()`, then check
    44	  whether the view changed.

Before measuring, please note the following two warnings:
1. **Do not apply excess force to the print with your calipers.**

The Truss is designed to resist such abuse as much as possible, but 3D printed plastics are elastic - applying excess force will deform the print and yield dimensions larger or smaller than actually printed.

Ideally the calipers should be exerting no expansive/compressive force on the print whatsoever - I personally let go of the clamping side entirely to achieve this, letting the print push the calipers back if necessary.
If your calipers have thumb-wheel rollers, do not use them to exert excess force during measurement.
2. Measure with the calipers parallel to the dimension you are measuring - excessively angled calipers will fail to measure the dimension correctly.

Fixed. The red box wasn't from the new markup — a dormant scaffolding rule started matching.

## Root cause

`src/styles/elements/form.css` carried a leftover debug rule from the original scaffold:

```css
fieldset > ul {
  background-color: red;
  display: inline;
}
```

It matched nothing before, because step 5's seating-rules `<ul>` lived in the step's `<div class="stack">`. When the inner-jaws guidance moved inside the `<fieldset>` in the previous change, the `<ul>` became a direct child of the fieldset — so the rule activated. The box was *small* precisely because `display: inline` shrinks the background to the inline box, which is also why the list's layout was wrong.

## Change

- Removed the whole `fieldset > ul` rule — both the red background and the bogus `display: inline`.
- Also removed the same leftover `background-color: red` from the `::marker` rule in `text.css`. It's a no-op property there (browsers only honour a small set of properties on `::marker`), but it's the same debugging leftover and would bite if that ever changed.

No other debug colours remain in `src/**/*.css`, and no test referenced either rule.

## Verification

In the browser at Q5, on the seating-rules list:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `display` | `inline` | `block` |
| `background-color` | `red` | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` |
| `::marker` background | `red` | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` |
| Rendered box | small, red | 656 × 168 px, 3 items |

`typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `build` and the full suite (364 tests) all pass.

## The bug

in `src/domain/validation.ts` compared the **signed** difference:

```ts
if (outer - inner > MAX_DIVERGENCE_MM) { … }
```

So a 5 mm gap warned when outer was the longer reading (`5 > 2`) but not when inner was (`-5 > 2` is false). The function's own doc comment already said order shouldn't matter — "only the size of the gap between them is judged" — so the code simply didn't match its stated intent.

Fixed by comparing the gap itself, and reporting that same magnitude in the message:

```ts
const gap = Math.abs(outer - inner)
if (gap > MAX_DIVERGENCE_MM) {
  warnings.push(divergence(gap))
}
```

export function checkAxisPair(outer: number, inner: number): readonly MeasurementWarning[] {
  const warnings: MeasurementWarning[] = []

  /*
   * The *size* of the gap, not its sign: the reading order is not evidence of
   * anything (see above), so an inner span 5mm longer than the outer one is the

   * just the same. Comparing the signed difference would silently accept every
   * reversed pair.

  const gap = Math.abs(outer - inner)

  }

  const implausible = checkReading(outer) ?? checkReading(inner)
  if (implausible !== null) {
    warnings.push(implausible)
  }

  return warnings
}

Currently step 7 of the quad calibration flow is unpredictable in its printer saving behavior.

- All names entered show the error "A printer called '...' is already saved" when saving. The printer info does seem to be saved even when this error shows.
- It seems to save all entered values within the session - for example if I let the above error occur for names "test1", "test2", and "test3", open the app in a separate tab, enter the edit printers menu, delete all the saved printers, and save a new printer "test4", all values (test1 through test4) are re-saved.

The intended behavior is as follows:
- The user types a printer name into the textbox. 
- As the user types a name into the textbox, it should check that a printer of the same name does not exist in the local storage list, showing a warning if it does.
- There should be no separate save button; instead the next step button should function as the save button which saves the printer name and its extrapolation factor on proceeding.
  As such, the next button should be disabled when the printer name in the textbox is a duplicate of an existing printer.
- Once the user proceeds to the next step (and saves the printer in the process), they should not be able to edit this saved value if they return from the next step using the back button. Disable the back button on the next step.

Step 7 is reworked to the behaviour you described.

## Root cause of the reported symptoms

The step had **both** a *Save printer* button and a *Next* button, and the save button wrote the record while the field kept the name. So:

1. Press *Save printer* with "test1" → written successfully. **The name field still said "test1", which now existed** → the live collision warning fired immediately ("A printer called test1 is already saved"). That's the "error shows but the info is saved" — it was saved, on the press before.
2. Press *Save again* →

genuinely collided → the hard error, quoting the record just written.
3. Because every name went in on its own press, `test1`–`test3` really were in storage. The "re-saved" behaviour afterwards is a separate, pre-existing trait: the repository keeps an in-memory list and writes the **whole** list on every change, with no cross-tab sync — so an older tab writes its stale copy back over another tab's deletions.

## What it does now

| | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Name entry | Typing checks the repository on every keystroke; a name already in use shows *(and the input is

)*: "A printer called *Rig One* is already saved. Names are unique and not case-sensitive, so choose another name to continue." |
| Saving | **No save button.** Next *is* the save: it writes the printer with the full-precision factor, then advances. Typing writes nothing. |
| Duplicate | Next stays disabled with the reason "Enter a printer name that is not already saved to continue." |
| Going back | Q8 has **no Back control**, so the saved name and factor can't be revisited. |

Verified in the browser, walking the real flow: typing "Rig One" character-by-character left the input connected and focused and storage empty; Next wrote `{"name":"Rig One","extrapolationFactor":0.9997272727272728}` and landed on step 8 with **no Back**; re-entering the flow and typing "rig one" showed the warning, disabled Next, and left storage untouched; a different name cleared it.

## Implementation notes

- The gate stays a **pure function of the draft**, per the project's existing rule: the Q7 screen mirrors the readiness fact into the draft (

, renamed from `printerSaved`) exactly as the degraded-mode skip already does. No engine or gate-registry coupling to storage was introduced.
-
performs the write for Q7 only, then calls

. If the write somehow fails (another tab taking the name between the last keystroke and the press) it closes the gate so the reason appears, rather than leaving Next inert.
- Degraded mode is unchanged: the field is hidden, the gate is skipped, the banner shows, and advancing stores nothing.
- **Choice to flag:** you asked to *disable* the Back button on Q8; I **removed** it, because that's this codebase's existing way of saying "no way back" (the final step does the same with Next) and a permanently greyed button with no story reads worse than its absence. Say the word if you'd rather see it visible-but-disabled.

## Verification

`typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`,

and the full suite (**367 tests**) pass. Tests updated/added: the engine's back-chain invariant now records `Q8` as the one deliberate gap; the collision test now asserts the warning, the disabled Next, and that **nothing is written while typing or while blocked**; and the results-screen test asserts there is no Back. PRD §9.3, §12 and the decision log (new #27) and

T28 were updated to match.

One thing I did **not** change: the multi-tab write-back described above (stale tab resurrecting another tab's deleted records). It's inherent to the current storage design and outside this step. I can add cross-tab re-sync via a
event listener if you want it.

Step 7 is reworked to the behaviour you described.

## Root cause of the reported symptoms

The step had **both** a *Save printer* button and a *Next* button, and the save button wrote the record while the field kept the name. So:

1. Press *Save printer* with "test1" → written successfully. **The name field still said "test1", which now existed** → the live collision warning fired immediately ("A printer called test1 is already saved"). That's the "error shows but the info is saved" — it was saved, on the press before.
2. Press *Save again* → `add` genuinely collided → the hard error, quoting the record just written.
3. Because every name went in on its own press, `test1`–`test3` really were in storage. The "re-saved" behaviour afterwards is a separate, pre-existing trait: the repository keeps an in-memory list and writes the **whole** list on every change, with no cross-tab sync — so an older tab writes its stale copy back over another tab's deletions.

## What it does now

| | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Name entry | Typing checks the repository on every keystroke; a name already in use shows *(and the input is `aria-invalid`)*: "A printer called *Rig One* is already saved. Names are unique and not case-sensitive, so choose another name to continue." |
| Saving | **No save button.** Next *is* the save: it writes the printer with the full-precision factor, then advances. Typing writes nothing. |
| Duplicate | Next stays disabled with the reason "Enter a printer name that is not already saved to continue." |
| Going back | Q8 has **no Back control**, so the saved name and factor can't be revisited. |

Verified in the browser, walking the real flow: typing "Rig One" character-by-character left the input connected and focused and storage empty; Next wrote `{"name":"Rig One","extrapolationFactor":0.9997272727272728}` and landed on step 8 with **no Back**; re-entering the flow and typing "rig one" showed the warning, disabled Next, and left storage untouched; a different name cleared it.

## Implementation notes

- The gate stays a **pure function of the draft**, per the project's existing rule: the Q7 screen mirrors the readiness fact into the draft (`CHECKS.printerNameReady`, renamed from `printerSaved`) exactly as the degraded-mode skip already does. No engine or gate-registry coupling to storage was introduced.
- `StepScreen.advance()` performs the write for Q7 only, then calls `engine.next()`. If the write somehow fails (another tab taking the name between the last keystroke and the press) it closes the gate so the reason appears, rather than leaving Next inert.
- Degraded mode is unchanged: the field is hidden, the gate is skipped, the banner shows, and advancing stores nothing.
- **Choice to flag:** you asked to *disable* the Back button on Q8; I **removed** it, because that's this codebase's existing way of saying "no way back" (the final step does the same with Next) and a permanently greyed button with no story reads worse than its absence. Say the word if you'd rather see it visible-but-disabled.

## Verification

`typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `build` and the full suite (**367 tests**) pass. Tests updated/added: the engine's back-chain invariant now records `Q8` as the one deliberate gap; the collision test now asserts the warning, the disabled Next, and that **nothing is written while typing or while blocked**; and the results-screen test asserts there is no Back. PRD §9.3, §12 and the decision log (new #27) and `BUILD-PLAN.md` T28 were updated to match.

One thing I did **not** change: the multi-tab write-back described above (stale tab resurrecting another tab's deleted records). It's inherent to the current storage design and outside this step. I can add cross-tab re-sync via a `storage` event listener if you want it.

children.text: ### T28 — Quad factor step Q7 (compute + mandatory save gate)
**Size:** L · **Depends on:** T27, T06, T08, T07 · **Unblocks:** T30, T33

**Context:** PRD §9.3, §12, decisions 9–10, 15 — display the factor at 10dp, then require a unique name and a successful save before the user may continue. A collision is a hard block, and because flow state is not persisted, its error copy must state the recovery path explicitly (Exit → delete the record → restart, losing all eight measurements) or users will read it as a bug. When storage is unavailable the gate is skipped as unsatisfiable, the banner is shown, and the factor is still displayed so the user can write it down.
- [x] T28.1 Compute and display the extrapolation factor (10dp)
- [x] T28.2 Implement the name field with live uniqueness feedback against the repository
- [x] T28.3 Implement the collision hard block including the explicit data-loss recovery copy
- [x] T28.4 Implement the storage-unavailable path: skip the gate, show the banner, still show the factor
- [x] T28.5 Gate Next on a successful save, or on degraded mode
- [x] T28.6 Tests: save success, collision block, degraded mode, factor formatting

> **Note (T28.4).** Degraded mode marks `CHECKS.printerSaved` from `onMount` rather than teaching the gate registry about storage. The gate stays a pure function of the draft, and the *reason* the check is satisfied is documented at the call site. The name field and save button are hidden entirely, so there is no field the user can fill in that silently does nothing.
### T29 — Results screen (shared by both flows)
**Size:** L · **Depends on:** T16, T05, T06, T14 · **Unblocks:** T30, T32

**Context:** PRD §10, decision 8 — the slicer-ready percentage is the hero with copy-to-clipboard, but it must also be legible for manual transcription, because the clipboard does not cross devices when a user measures at the printer and edits the slicer elsewhere. Details differ per flow, so the component is variant-driven. Recalculation must use full precision, never the displayed rounded ratio.
- [x] T29.1 Implement the hero percentage with copy control and a transcribable presentation
- [x] T29.2 Implement the current slicer value input (default `100%`) with validation and soft range warnings
- [x] T29.3 Implement the details block for both variants — quad: 8-value average, X average, factor, ratio; single: 2 values, average, stored factor, extrapolated average
- [x] T29.4 Author the slicer-entry instructions content
- [x] T29.5 Recompute on current-value change at full precision
- [x] T29.6 Tests: both variants' details, precision behaviour, warnings on unusual current values

> **Note (T29.5).** The current slicer value is seeded from the draft with `untrack`, and the input owns it from then on. A tracked read there would rewrite the field while the user is typing. Recalculation itself uses the full-precision ratio, never the displayed 5dp form — the T29.6 test with a current value of 98 pins this (0.981875 × 0.98 → 96.224, which the rounded ratio gets wrong).
### T30 — Quad results integration and exit (Q8–Q9)
**Size:** M · **Depends on:** T28, T29, T15 · **Unblocks:** T32, T33
**Context:** PRD §9.3 — the save gate precedes the result (decision 9), and exit returns to the landing screen (decision 17). The exit-confirmation rule must hold from the first measurement onward.
- [x] T30.1 Wire Q7 → Q8 results using T29
- [x] T30.2 Implement the exit action returning to the landing screen
- [x] T30.3 Verify the exit-confirmation rule at every step from Q5 onward
- [x] T30.4 End-to-end test: full quad flow from landing to exit using Fixture B

> **Note (T30.3) — bug found by the end-to-end test.** Exit was implemented as the *fallback* for the Back slot in `StepChrome`, so it existed only on C1. From Q1 onward the only way out of a flow was to walk Back through every screen. PRD §9.2 (and the §14 acceptance table) require Back + Next + Exit on every step, with the confirmation conditioned on whether a measurement has been entered. The chrome now always renders Exit, and `requestExit` still decides whether to confirm — which is what makes C1–C2 and Q1–Q4 leave without a dialog.

> **Note (T30.4).** The end-to-end suite lives in `src/components/flow.e2e.test.tsx` and drives the real screens through the real engine with a storage double. This is the layer that caught both wiring bugs above: each component was correct in isolation, and the mistakes were in how they were connected.

const click = async (l) => { await l.evaluate((el) => el.click()); await page.waitForTimeout(70) }
const next = () => click(page.getByTestId('next'))

const heading = () => page.getByRole('heading', { level: 2 }).first().textContent()

await page.reload()
await page.waitForTimeout(500)
await click(page.getByTestId('start'))

// C1 is skipped when the "don't ask again" flag is set; pass it if it appears.

  await click(page.getByLabel(/digital calipers/))
  await click(page.getByLabel(/functional, calibrated printer/))
  await click(page.getByLabel(/modern slicer/))
  await next()
}

// C2 → the quick branch.
await click(page.getByLabel(/calibrated on this printer before/))
await next()

const out = { s1: await heading() }
await click(page.getByLabel(/^Rig One/))
await next()
await click(page.getByLabel(/Temperature settings/))
await click(page.getByLabel(/Pressure advance/))
await click(page.getByLabel(/Flow rate/))
await next()
await click(page.getByLabel(/no seams on the measurement faces/))
await next()
await click(page.getByLabel(/printed the calibrator/))
await next()
out.s5 = await heading()
await fill(/^X outer/i, '137.6'); await fill(/^X inner/i, '137.4')
await next()

out.s6 = await heading()
out.progress = await page.getByTestId('step-progress').textContent()
out.navButtons = await page.locator('section .row button').evaluateAll((els) => els.map((e) => e.textContent.trim()))
out.cancelCount = await page.getByTestId('exit').count()
out.hero = await page.getByTestId('hero-percentage').textContent()
out.backCount = await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Back' }).count()

await click(page.getByTestId('next'))
await page.waitForTimeout(250)
out.exitDialog = await page.getByTestId('exit-confirmation').count()
out.landed = (await page.getByTestId('start').count()) === 1
return out

if ((await page.getByLabel(/digital calipers/).count()) > 0) {

out.cancelCount = await page.getByTestId('exit').count()
